sub: The master lock against public exposure.

Overview.p: Block Public Access (BPA) is a master switch with four settings that stop buckets and objects from becoming public, at account or bucket level.
A master lock: even if someone opens a door by mistake, the lock keeps the public out.
A company turns on BPA for the whole account so no team can expose data by accident.

items: On by default for new buckets
BPA is checked with every request
It ignores public ACLs if enabled
It blocks public bucket policies if enabled
Turn it off only for special cases

Practical.p: Terminate or delete everything you created after practice to avoid charges.

items: Keep it on at account level
Use CloudFront with OAC instead of a public website bucket

Examples.p: use CloudFront with OAC and keep BPA on.

CLI Commands.p: IDs like i-0abc123 and sg-0abc123 are examples. Replace them with your real IDs.

items: Does BPA override a public policy?
Yes, when the matching option is on.
Account level applies to every bucket. The stricter setting wins.
